what: epList: retrieve lists of objects from enviPath
title: enviPathR: the R Client for the enviPath RESTful API
text: available elements object type can explored using epList. default, objects listed available packages, objects can listed specific package using argument pkg. example, possible retrieve pathways EAWAG-BBD package providing unique identifier. Similarly, supported enviPath object types can also explored way (see epTypes).
code: # List available packages pkg_df <- epList("package")  # Select reviewed packages to_keep <- pkg_df$reviewStatus == "reviewed" pkg_df <- pkg_df[to_keep, ]  # Remove lengthy description pkg_df$description <- NULL  # View list of packages kable(pkg_df) # Select desired package pkg_name <- "EAWAG-BBD" pkg_id <- pkg_df$id[pkg_df$name == pkg_name]  # List pathways from desired package path_df <- epList("pathway", pkg = pkg_id)  # View list of pathways path_df |>     head() |>     kable()

what: epLink: map between different types of objects
title: enviPathR: the R Client for the enviPath RESTful API
text: Links object types can retrieved epLink, takes origin target object types, optional initial values argument init. latter recommended prevent search exploding. Multiple initial values can also used, output represents many--many mapping. Similarly, supported enviPath object types can also linked way (see epTypes).
code: # Define reaction of interest rxn_id <- "2b6bbcc5-77f4-4bed-92a9-731cdc978f6a"  # Map desired reaction to related compounds (educts and products) rxn2cpd <- epLink("reaction", "compound", init = rxn_id)  # View reaction-to-compound mapping kable(rxn2cpd) # Select pathways of interest path_ids <- path_df$id[1:2]  # Map desired pathways to related compounds (nodes) path2cpd <- epLink("pathway", "compound", init = path_ids, pkg = pkg_id)  # View pathway-to-compound mapping kable(path2cpd)

title: enviPathR: the R Client for the enviPath RESTful API
text: enviPath provides set pre-trained models chemical fate prediction half-life persistence known unknown compounds given SMILES representation. available models can retrieved epList. Pathway prediction performed epModel, uses enviFormer model default. output list contains two data frames representing nodes (compounds) edges (reactions) predicted pathway, respectively. Different model settings can specified argument setting. example, PEPPER model can used also returns half-lime estimates predicted degradation steps. Remarkably, output epModel can directly converted igraph object visualised pathway graph. , plot function base R used simplicity, ggraph package recommended advanced graph visualisation.  mentioned , ggraph can used create informative visualisations including organised layouts additional aesthetic layers.
code: # List available model settings set_df <- epList("setting")  # View list kable(set_df) # Define smiles of interest smiles <- "ClC(Cl)=C(Cl)Cl"  # Perform pathway prediction with enviFormer former_out <- epModel(smiles)  # View compounds in predicted pathway kable(former_out$nodes) # View reactions in predicted pathway kable(former_out$edges) # Set id for PEPPER model setting set_name <- "Global Setting - ECC and App Domain - PEPPER" set_id <- set_df$id[set_df$name == set_name]  # Perform pathway prediction with PEPPER pepper_out <- epModel(smiles, set_id)  # View compounds in predicted pathway kable(pepper_out$nodes) # View reactions in predicted pathway kable(pepper_out$edges) # Convert model output to igraph object path_graph <- graph_from_data_frame(     pepper_out$edges,     vertices = pepper_out$nodes )  # Visualise predicted pathway plot(path_graph) library(ggraph)  ggraph(path_graph, layout = "sugiyama") +     geom_edge_link(aes(colour = probability), arrow = arrow(type = "closed")) +     geom_node_point(size = 3) +     geom_node_text(aes(label = name), vjust = 2) +     scale_edge_colour_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), low = "white", high = "red") +     theme_graph(base_family = "")

code: if( is_active ){ library(igraph) library(ggraph)  # Perform login with your credentials epLogin(username, password)  # Define smiles of interest smiles <- "ClC(Cl)=C(Cl)Cl"  # Perform pathway prediction with enviFormer former_out <- epModel(smiles)  # List available model settings set_df <- epList("setting")  # View some model settings head(set_df)  # Set id for PEPPER model setting set_name <- "Global Setting - ECC and App Domain - PEPPER" set_id <- set_df$id[set_df$name == set_name]  # Perform pathway prediction with PEPPER pepper_out <- epModel(smiles, set_id)  # Convert model output to igraph object path_graph <- graph_from_data_frame(     pepper_out$edges,     vertices = pepper_out$nodes )  # Visualise predicted pathway plot(path_graph)  # Visualise with ggraph ggraph(path_graph, layout = "sugiyama") +     geom_edge_link(         aes(colour = probability),         arrow = arrow(type = "closed")     ) +     geom_node_point(size = 3) +     geom_node_text(aes(label = name), vjust = 2) +     scale_edge_colour_continuous(         limits = c(0, 1), low = "white", high = "red"     ) +     theme_graph(base_family = "") } #>  #> Attaching package: ‘igraph’ #> The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’: #>  #>     decompose, spectrum #> The following object is masked from ‘package:base’: #>  #>     union #> Loading required package: ggplot2 #> Hi nature lover, welcome to enviPath!
